bug_description.original: The function opj_tcd_mct_decode() contains insufficient checks to verify that MCT can be performed safely, potentially leading to a security vulnerability.
bug_description.normalized: In the staged vulnerable OpenJPEG revision c67e1cd73f6c1fca081f5445af4f65b240c40edc, the saved 106-byte raw J2K witness parses SIZ image bounds `(0,2)-(12,12)`, a 4x4 tile grid of 3x3 tiles from origin `(0,0)`, `Csiz=3`, and component sampling factors `dx={1,1,33}`. COD also enables built-in irreversible MCT with `mct=1`, `numresolutions=5`, and `qmfbid=0`, and the first SOT selects tile-part `Isot=0`. Because the fuzzer asks to decode the whole 12x10 image, tile 0 stays on the whole-tile path. `opj_tcd_init_tile()` makes tile 0 bounds `(0,2)-(3,3)`: components 0 and 1 keep extent `(0,2)-(3,3)`, but component 2 becomes `(0,2)-(1,3)` and is later allocated exactly one 32-bit sample, i.e. 4 bytes, matching the saved ASan allocation stack. In `opj_tcd_mct_decode()`, the whole-tile branch computes `l_samples=3` from component 0's `minimum_num_resolutions - 1` extent, but the safety check still compares `resno_decoded` resolution 0 extents instead. On this witness, resolution 0 collapses all three components to `(0,1)-(1,1)`, so the guard sees zero samples for each component and falls through. `opj_mct_decode_real()` is then called with `n=3` and component 2's one-sample buffer, and the second scalar-loop iteration reads `c2[1]` 4 bytes past that 4-byte region, producing the saved AddressSanitizer `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4`. The fix commit cc893a4ebfaf8c42cf1221ac82c83df91e77340b adds a dedicated `whole_tile_decoding` dimension check that compares the same `minimum_num_resolutions - 1` extents used for `l_samples`.

source.description: First project statement that materializes vulnerability-relevant geometry from the SIZ marker. The surrounding SIZ reads make the staged witness a 12x10 image with bounds `(0,2)-(12,12)`, which later forces tile 0 to be only one sample row tall.
source.value_from: The libFuzzer harness recognizes `gt_results/arvo_3305/poc` as raw J2K because it begins with `FF 4F`, then passes its 106 bytes into `opj_read_header()`. Static parsing of the saved codestream shows SIZ `Xsiz=12`, `Ysiz=12`, `X0=0`, `Y0=2`, `XTsiz=3`, `YTsiz=3`, `XT0=0`, `YT0=0`, `Csiz=3`, component records `0f 01 01 | 09 01 01 | 0f 21 01`, COD `mct=1`, `numresolutions=5`, `qmfbid=0`, and SOT `Isot=0`.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. `opj_mct_decode_real()` reads component 2 as if it contained three float samples, but on the crashing tile the buffer holds only one 32-bit sample.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4` at `src/lib/openjp2/mct.c:433:25` and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of a 4-byte region allocated for the tile component buffer.

root_cause.description: Wrong-basis safety check in the whole-tile MCT path. The vulnerable code validates component compatibility using `resno_decoded` extents even though the whole-tile branch sizes buffers and computes `l_samples` from `minimum_num_resolutions - 1` extents.
root_cause.note: For this witness, `resno_decoded = 0` makes `res_comp0`, `res_comp1`, and `res_comp2` all refer to resolution-0 extents `(0,1)-(1,1)`, so `l_res_samples` and the comparison products are all zero and the `if` condition is false. The upstream patch fixes this by checking whole-tile extents inside the `whole_tile_decoding` branch.

tainted_value_origin.description: The dangerous tainted value is component 2's horizontal sampling factor `dx = 33`, parsed directly from the witness's SIZ marker. Combined with the staged image and tile geometry, it shrinks tile 0's whole-tile component-2 extent to `(0,2)-(1,3)` while components 0 and 1 stay `(0,2)-(3,3)`.

parser_admitted.description: The staged 106-byte witness has already passed format dispatch as raw J2K and entered OpenJPEG's codestream parser. `opj_read_header()` must accept the stream before the vulnerable SIZ/COD parsing and tile decode path can execute.

coarse_trace.summary: OpenJPEG parses the witness headers, materializing image bounds `(0,2)-(12,12)`, a 4x4 tile grid of 3x3 tiles, three components with component 2 subsampled to `dx=33`, irreversible built-in MCT, five resolutions, and tile-part `Isot=0`.
The decode window covers the whole image; tile init turns tile 0 into bounds `(0,2)-(3,3)`, sets `resno_decoded=0` and `minimum_num_resolutions=5`, and keeps `whole_tile_decoding` enabled.
The whole-tile allocation path sizes component 2 from its `minimum_num_resolutions - 1` extent and allocates only one 32-bit sample, i.e. 4 bytes.

The whole-tile MCT path computes `l_samples = 3` from component 0 but validates only `resno_decoded` resolution 0, where all three components collapse to zero samples, so the mismatch is missed and `opj_mct_decode_real()` is called.
On the second scalar-loop iteration, `c2[1]` reads 4 bytes past component 2's 4-byte allocation and triggers the saved ASan heap-buffer-overflow.

fine_trace.note: Source. The first SIZ reads materialize image bounds `Xsiz=12`, `Ysiz=12`, `X0siz=0`, `Y0siz=2`, i.e. image rectangle `(0,2)-(12,12)`. That 12x10 image origin later makes tile 0 only one sample row tall.

The same SIZ marker stores tile geometry `XTsiz=3`, `YTsiz=3`, `XT0siz=0`, `YT0siz=0`, and `Csiz=3`. Since `tw = ceil((12 - 0) / 3) = 4` and `th = ceil((12 - 0) / 3) = 4`, OpenJPEG will therefore decode a 4x4 grid of 3x3 tiles anchored at codestream origin `(0,0)`.

In the component records, components 0 and 1 keep `dx=1`, but component 2 gets `dx=33` with `dy=1`. This is the tainted sampling mismatch that later shrinks component 2's tile-0 whole-tile extent to one sample.
The COD marker sets `mct=1`, so `opj_tcd_mct_decode()` will not return at `if (! l_tcp->mct)` and the built-in 3-component MCT path stays enabled.

The SPCod byte `0x04` is incremented to `numresolutions=5`. With decoder reduce 0, tile init later sets `minimum_num_resolutions=5`, so whole-tile code will use index 4 while the vulnerable guard still uses `resno_decoded=0`.

The same COD payload sets `qmfbid=0`, selecting the irreversible floating-point transform. If execution reaches MCT, `opj_tcd_mct_decode()` will call `opj_mct_decode_real()` instead of the integer path.

Because step 1's image size is only 12x10, the fuzzer's width/height clamp at 1024 does not reduce it; `opj_set_decode_area()` therefore stores the full image window `(0,2)-(12,12)` in the output image. Later tile decode uses those bounds as `win_x0..win_y1`.
When the first tile-part header is read, the SOT `Isot` field sets `p_tile_no=0`. The crashing decode therefore operates on tile 0.

In `opj_tcd_init_tile()` for `p_tile_no=0`, `p=0` and `q=0`, so intersecting the top-left tile from the 4x4 grid in step 2 with the image rectangle from step 1 yields tile 0 bounds `(0,2)-(3,3)`. Tile 0 is only one row tall.

Tile init sets each component's `resno_decoded = 0`. Because step 5 gave `numresolutions=5` and decode reduce is 0, the same loop sets `minimum_num_resolutions = 5`, so whole-tile code uses resolution index 4 and `opj_tcd_is_whole_tilecomp_decoding()` gets `shift = 0`.
For components 0 and 1 (`dx=1`, `dy=1`), dividing tile 0 by the sampling factors leaves tile-component coordinates `(0,2)-(3,3)`. Their full-resolution whole-tile extent is therefore 3 samples.
For component 2, the same formula uses `dx=33`, so tile 0 becomes `(0,2)-(1,3)`: one sample wide and one sample high.
At the start of `opj_tcd_decode_tile()`, OpenJPEG stores `p_tile_no=0` and the full-image window `(0,2)-(12,12)` into `p_tcd->{tcd_tileno,win_x0,win_y0,win_x1,win_y1}`.

The actual whole-tile predicate now evaluates with step 13's full-image window, step 10's `shift=0`, and the tile-component bounds from steps 11-12. For every component, `tcx0..tcy1` exactly cover the tile component, so `opj_tcd_is_whole_tilecomp_decoding()` returns true and `p_tcd->whole_tile_decoding` stays enabled.

In the whole-tile allocation loop for component 2, `l_res = tilec->resolutions[minimum_num_resolutions - 1] = resolutions[4]`. With step 10's index 4 and step 12's component-2 coordinates `(0,2)-(1,3)`, `res_w=1` and `res_h=1`, so `tilec->data_size_needed = 1 * 1 * sizeof(OPJ_UINT32) = 4` bytes.
Allocation context. AddressSanitizer reports that the invalid read landed 0 bytes to the right of a 4-byte region allocated from this call chain, matching step 15's one-sample component-2 buffer.

In `opj_tcd_mct_decode()`'s whole-tile branch, `l_tile_comp` initially points to component 0. Using the same whole-tile index `minimum_num_resolutions - 1 = 4`, component 0's extent from step 11 is `(0,2)-(3,3)`, so `l_samples = (3 - 0) * (3 - 2) = 3`. Component 1 shares the same 3-sample extent.

Root cause. The guard builds `res_comp0`, `res_comp1`, and `res_comp2` from `resno_decoded = 0` instead of the whole-tile index 4. For this witness, `opj_tcd_init_tile()` computed resolution-0 extents `(0,1)-(1,1)` for all three components: tile 0's one-row height collapses to zero after the four-level `ceildivpow2` reduction. Thus `l_res_samples = 0`, both comparison products are also 0, and all three `resno_decoded` values are equal, so the `if (...)` condition is false even though steps 15-17 already established 1-sample vs 3-sample whole-tile buffers.

Because step 2 gave `numcomps=3`, step 4 enabled MCT, step 6 selected `qmfbid=0`, step 14 kept whole-tile decoding, and step 18 did not reject, the decoder calls `opj_mct_decode_real()` with `l_samples=3` and component 2's one-sample buffer.

depends_on.via: p_tcd->image->comps[0].resno_decoded != p_tcd->image->comps[1].resno_decoded || p_tcd->image->comps[0].resno_decoded != p_tcd->image->comps[2].resno_decoded || (OPJ_SIZE_T)(res_comp1->x1 - res_comp1->x0) * (OPJ_SIZE_T)(res_comp1->y1 - res_comp1->y0) != l_res_samples || (OPJ_SIZE_T)(res_comp2->x1 - res_comp2->x0) * (OPJ_SIZE_T)(res_comp2->y1 - res_comp2->y0) != l_res_samples

fine_trace.note: Sink. With `n=3`, the scalar loop's first iteration (`i=0`) reads the only in-bounds float from component 2, and the second iteration (`i=1`) evaluates `c2[1]`. That 4-byte load lands exactly at the first byte past the 4-byte region from step 16, matching the saved ASan `READ of size 4` at `mct.c:433`.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports that the invalid read happened 0 bytes to the right of a 4-byte region allocated through `opj_alloc_tile_component_data()` -> `opj_aligned_alloc_n()`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: staged sanitizer_trace.txt and reproduction_report.json; fixed image was not dynamically validated in Stage 02

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. The allocation stack proves component 2 was sized from whole-tile index `minimum_num_resolutions - 1`, while the root cause is the later `opj_tcd_mct_decode` guard validating `resno_decoded` index 0, where this witness collapses all three components to zero samples.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch is source-consistent with the traced root cause because it adds a dedicated `whole_tile_decoding` dimension check using `minimum_num_resolutions - 1`, but Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_3305 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed `poc` to `opj_decompress_fuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4` in `opj_mct_decode_real` with stack `opj_tcd_mct_decode -> opj_tcd_decode_tile`.

format.name: 106-byte raw JPEG 2000 codestream
format.contract: Exactly the staged 106-byte witness stored as `poc` (sha256 `3af76c33ef50edc3dd1ecbe5565b81a76b2c9388b0b935d0bdd58e0df0dcab25`). The verified trigger is this exact raw J2K codestream, whose SIZ marker materializes image bounds `(0,2)-(12,12)`, tile size `3x3` from origin `(0,0)` with `tw=4` and `th=4`, `Csiz=3`, and component sampling factors `XRsiz={1,1,33}`; whose COD marker sets `mct=1`, `numresolutions=5`, `qmfbid=0`; and whose first SOT sets `Isot=0`. On this witness, tile 0 stays on the whole-tile path, component 2 is allocated one 32-bit sample, `opj_tcd_mct_decode()` still computes `l_samples=3` from component 0, and `opj_mct_decode_real()` over-reads `c2[1]`. Stage 02 does not establish a broader trigger class beyond this witness.
